report.summary: Fixed the hardware panic: the dashboard no longer calls app_display_init() a second time (two setup tasks fighting one LVGL port) — it waits on app_display_ready() and then draws; also wired the spec's wake sources into the screen-dim logic. Builds at 2.94 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: The panic is the structural bug I had flagged as a risk two rounds ago: app_display_init() starts the display in its own task, and heating_ui_init() called it AGAIN, so two setup tasks drove one LVGL port — the log shows 'LVGL: Stopped LVGL task' immediately after the second add, then the assert. The double 'Display setup started' / 'Display initialized' pairs in every log so far were the same fault.

Fixed at the owner, not by reordering callers: app_display now publishes app_display_ready()/app_display_failed() and turns a second app_display_init() into a warning. heating_ui_init() waits for ready (30 s bound) instead of sleeping 1.5 s and racing — a fixed sleep is exactly what lost this race on hardware while passing on the emulator.

Went through the rest of the boot log for genuine product issues: the remaining errors are board/environment (no SD card, the camera probe falling back from SC101IOT to OV3660, an emulator RF-calibration miss) and not firmware faults. The one product-visible gap was the spec's wake sources for the screen dim (touch/button/wake word/MQTT), which existed for touch only; heating_ui_poke() now marks a heard command, a wake word, a setpoint, an MQTT state message and a link change as activity.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2ccf40 (2936640 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; check_code clean on the five edited sources

openQuestions: The remaining boot-log errors are environment/board (SD card absent, camera sensor probe fallback to OV3660, emulator RF calibration); nothing points at the firmware.
Whether the RGB panel's buffers (800x480, 40-line double buffer, no bounce buffer) are right in practice still needs a real screen.
